top: This register lists what a client must confirm for the model to be defensible — not what the model computes. It deliberately surfaces 0 coefficients that are hardcoded in the calculation path and editable nowhere in the interface. They materially drive the euro result, so until now the question “where does that number come from?” had no answer, even internally. Surfacing them is not a criticism of the model — every model has coefficients; the defect was that they were unseeable.Where these values come from. AgentCase ships with defaults for the metric anchors and for the model’s internal coefficients. These are engineering estimates: no study, dataset or delivery record is cited for them, and they are not benchmarks. That is what this register is for — each becomes a confirmed input once validated against the client’s own records. Rows marked PC4 unvalidated and PC5 embedded are the ones still awaiting that confirmation.Items to confirm89Editable nowhere (PC5)0Confirmed / waived (items)0%Confirmed by € weight0%Glass ceiling confirmed0%of the 25% ceiling’s weightTwo gauges, two questions. € coverage says how much of the figure rests on unverified values. Ceiling coverage says how much of the thesis does — the artefact-by-artefact claim that a human signature is irreducible. Telemetry cannot measure this and a simulation cannot validate it: only the people who sign the certification can.Y3 savings rest on 100% unconfirmed input weight. Item count is shown alongside because a high item percentage with low weighted coverage means the easy things were confirmed and the load-bearing ones were not.
tr: perfRel() upper clampCaps how far velocity/productivity may exceed the ramp-implied uplift. At 1.4 every anchor overshot its target until the v16.1 clamp (F9).
defaultPerfUplift() factorScales the reference uplift against which every ramp is measured. Moves all velocity, DORA and throughput readings.
Verification tax hard capCeiling on the share of savings deducted for review effort.
Verification tax base rateReview need before supervision credit. Multiplied by average human supervision (overlay) or netted against it.
Quality premium capMaximum rework multiplier applied for AI-authored code quality risk (EV-23).
Decision-bar quality weightConverts the quality premium into a decision-intelligence penalty, capped at 0.15.
HRI ramp floorWorst-case adoption drag: a zero-readiness organisation still realises 60% of the ramp.
HRI ramp slopeHow much readiness buys back. floor + slope x HRI/100.
Supervision share capSupervision FTE never exceeds half the residual team, whatever the supervision matrix says.
Supervision share factorsupShare = min(0.5, avgHumanSup x 0.5). Sets how much of the retained team supervises rather than produces.
Context glass factorMultiplies effective automation for the engagement context.
Ramp cap (%)Hard ceiling on every annual ramp.
Ramp speedScales every annual ramp before the cap.
CC maturity multiplierMultiplies effective automation by the target collective-competence tier.
Lifecycle auto postureMultiplies effective automation by the blended product profile.
Computed glass ceiling (%)Effort-weighted irreducible human supervision. Caps effective automation at 100 - ceiling.

Transitional setup headcount (FTE)Sizes the "Agentic Setup" row of the Team-out table. Display only — its € is already counted inside the Setup budget, not added on top.
Agent capacity factorScales the "(indicative)" agent-capacity read-out only. Deliberately isolated from vFTE/savings by design (effort-conservation invariant).
AI-FinOps flat FTEOne illustrative row inside the Agentic Run team breakdown. Does not independently feed the top-level run cost.
